sources.note: Ran the hybrid+EV filter (37 listings) and an all-fuel pass sorted by mileage plus a model-filtered efficient-gas pass. Vehicle detail pages returned a Cloudflare bot challenge, so VIN/accident data is missing for Cars.com-sourced rows.
Hybrid+Electric fuel filter (104 listings across 5 pages) plus a gasoline pass sorted by deal score with a 120k mileage cap. Best source for deal ratings, IMV deltas, VINs and title/accident data.

Denver cta with pipe-OR queries for hybrid/prius/leaf/volt/ct200h/niro/ioniq/insight and a separate efficient-gas query. Many private gas listings had implausible prices (2024-2025 cars at $6-7k) and were screened out as likely bait.

minPrice+sortBy combination returned a stuck 3-tile grid; dropping those params fixed it. Ran prius, nissan leaf, chevy volt, toyota corolla and honda civic queries with scrolling, then opened 6 detail pages for mileage and photos. Several results were dealer cross-posts already captured on CarGurus and were deduped.
Verified inventory floor: cheapest Prius is $14,590 and cheapest Leaf is $17,990. Nothing under $10,000 nationwide.

Buy-It-Now search ran, but the 100-mile radius filter did not constrain results (everything returned as 'Located in United States'). Nothing verifiably local that was not already found elsewhere; remainder were salvage or out-of-state fly-and-drive listings.
Ran prius, nissan leaf and toyota corolla queries. Only the Aurora 2016 Prius c cleared the bar; the rest were 145k+ mile or pre-2010 cars.
Sorted the 100-mile Denver inventory by price ascending: cheapest unit is $15,560. Nothing under $10,000.

Searched near Denver/Aurora with no fuel restriction and sorted price low-to-high nationwide: cheapest unit is $12,282 (2019 Sentra, Charleston SC). Nothing under $10,000 anywhere in their inventory today.
Deliberately not searched - 27 qualifying candidates were found inside the 100-mile radius, so there was no reason to stretch to Utah (350+ miles) this run.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a genuinely roomy rear bench and easy-to-reach lower LATCH anchors; rear-facing seat fits without pushing the front passenger forward much.
listings.nextAction: Listed today and priced ~$4.2k under CarGurus market - call the dealer this morning, ask why (fleet/auction car? cosmetic damage?) and book a pre-purchase inspection before deposit.
listings.why: Lowest-mileage sub-$10k car found this run with a clean title, 0 accidents and a huge below-market delta. 32 mpg combined clears the gas floor and Sentras of this era are cheap to maintain.

listings.carSeatNotes: Corolla rear seat is one of the roomiest in the compact class; rear-facing installs cleanly and the wide door opening helps with a toddler.
listings.nextAction: Private seller, listed a day ago - message for the VIN and a photo of the title, then run a paid history report before driving to Lakewood.
listings.why: Cheapest genuinely reliable 34-mpg car on the board. LE Eco trim is the high-mpg Corolla, 5-star NHTSA overall, and Corolla drivetrains routinely run past 250k.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan - the easiest car here for a rear-facing seat; deep rear footwell and full-size door opening, plus a big trunk for the daycare bag and stroller.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 5 miles away - request the free Carfax link and ask for records on the hybrid battery cooling filter and any 2013 Fusion recall work.
listings.why: 41 mpg in a 5-star midsize sedan, clean title, no accidents, $1,567 under market and closest to home. Best family-shaped car per dollar this run.

listings.carSeatNotes: Rear seat is tight and the 2011-2015 Volt has a two-seat rear bench with a center console - fine for one child seat, awkward if a second passenger sits back there.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for a photo of the dash showing current electric range, plus the title, before driving to Golden.
listings.why: A 38-mile electric range covers the whole Lone Tree + daycare loop on Level 1 charging, with a gas engine for road trips. 5-star NHTSA and lower miles than the dealer Volts.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatchback body means an upright rear seat and a high roofline - easy to lift a child in, and the hatch swallows daycare gear.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 1 accident on record, so ask for the Carfax damage detail and inspect the rear structure before committing.
listings.why: Biggest below-market delta of any hybrid here (-$2,846), 40 mpg, low miles for the year and a practical hatch shape. The single accident report is the only caveat.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Same tight 4-seat Volt cabin - workable for one rear-facing seat, verify front-passenger legroom with the seat installed.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 5 miles away - ask for the battery state-of-health readout and confirm the 8-year/100k battery warranty has not just expired on mileage.
listings.why: Dealer-backed Volt only 5 miles from home with a clean history. Slightly more money and miles than the Golden private-party car, but far less risk.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat - the most rear-facing room of anything on this list, and a flat floor if a second adult ever rides back there.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 3 open recall campaigns for this model year plus 1 accident reported; ask for recall completion receipts and the Carfax damage detail.
listings.why: Biggest cabin on the board at 40 mpg, 5-star NHTSA, $1,709 under market and still under Hyundai's 10-year hybrid battery warranty term for original owners.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Crossover-height hatchback: high hip point makes buckling a child seat much easier on your back, and the cargo area handles a stroller upright.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 157k miles, so make the deal contingent on a hybrid-system scan and ask for service records on the dual-clutch transmission.
listings.why: 49 mpg combined - the highest-mpg non-plug-in here - in the most family-friendly body style, clean title, no accidents. Mileage is the trade-off.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - a rear-facing seat will fit but expect to slide the front passenger seat well forward. Test-fit your actual seat before buying.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 1 accident reported and no title status shown; ask for the Carfax and confirm the title is clean before you go look at it.
listings.why: Cheapest 50-mpg car in the metro and Toyota hybrid reliability is the safest bet in the segment. Docked for size and the accident report.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a flat, wide rear bench and good door aperture - a rear-facing seat goes in easily and the hatch holds daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Ask the dealer to photograph the dash battery-capacity bars (12 = healthy) or run a LeafSpy report before you drive out.
listings.why: 2017 is the first Leaf year worth buying (30 kWh, ~107 mi new). Even at 70% health that is ~75 mi - triple your 25-mile workday - and Level 1 charging refills it overnight.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same easy Leaf hatchback layout - flat rear floor, wide doors, low lift-over for the child seat.
listings.nextAction: 70 miles away in Fort Collins - before making that drive, ask the seller for a photo of the battery bars and the charge percentage.
listings.why: Same generation and mileage as the Denver Leaf for a bit more money, but private-party. Only worth the trip if the battery bars come back at 11-12.

listings.title: Clean
listings.carSeatNotes: Tall hatch with an upright rear seat - very easy child-seat access, though the Energi battery eats a chunk of the cargo floor.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - 8 recall campaigns exist for this model year; ask for completion receipts, and check the plug-in battery still holds its ~21-mile range.
listings.why: By far the lowest mileage on this list (51,856) and a plug-in that would cover most of your daily loop on electricity. Priced near the top of budget and it is a 54-mile drive.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy compact rear bench with accessible LATCH anchors; rear-facing fits without crowding the driver.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - request the VIN and free Carfax (the detail page was bot-blocked today, so title/accident status is unconfirmed).
listings.why: Second Great-Deal Sentra of the run at a lower price than the Littleton car, only 70k miles. Useful backup if the Littleton one turns out to have a story.

listings.carSeatNotes: Rear seat is a little snug front-to-back for rear-facing; test-fit before buying, but the doors open wide and the seat backs are upright.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 7 miles away - 6 recall campaigns for this model year (mostly Takata-era), so ask for completion receipts.
listings.why: 5-star safety, 33 mpg and Mazda3s of this generation age well. Closest good gas car to home, though rear legroom is the weak point for a child seat.

listings.carSeatNotes: Ninth-gen Civic has a surprisingly deep rear footwell - rear-facing installs well and the low door sill is easy on your back.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for the VIN and title photo, and confirm the Takata airbag recall was completed before you view it.
listings.why: $6,000 for a 5-star, 32-mpg Civic is strong value and these engines are famously durable. Mileage is high but the maintenance bill will be low.

listings.carSeatNotes: Upright tall-hatch rear seat, very easy child-seat access; the plug-in battery raises the cargo floor.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 47 miles out - ask for the Carfax and confirm the plug-in battery still charges to full before making the drive.
listings.why: Cheaper way into a plug-in than the 2013 SEL, still a Good Deal rating. Higher miles and a long drive are the trade-offs.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact sedan - rear-facing fits but front-passenger legroom gets tight. Standard low-speed automatic emergency braking is a nice safety bonus at this price.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - zero open recalls, so focus on a pre-purchase inspection and ask for the Carfax.
listings.why: 36 mpg, zero open recalls, Mazda2 mechanicals under a Toyota warranty pedigree, and it came standard with automatic emergency braking - rare under $10k.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same roomy Sentra rear bench; 2019 SV adds forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking as standard - the best active-safety kit of the gas cars here.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - request the VIN and free Carfax; also confirm the CVT has service records, as this is the weak point on these.
listings.why: Newest car on the list and the only gas pick with standard automatic emergency braking. Top of budget, and CVT history matters.

listings.carSeatNotes: Best-in-class rear legroom for a compact - rear-facing goes in with room to spare and the doors open nearly square.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for the VIN and title photo before driving to Todd Creek, and get a pre-purchase inspection.
listings.why: Low-mileage 5-star Corolla with 32 mpg from a private seller - the most bulletproof drivetrain on this list. Priced near the top of budget for the miles.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat with excellent rear-facing clearance; trunk is reduced by the battery but still holds a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - ask whether the 10-year/100k plug-in battery warranty transferred, and confirm the charge port and 29-mile range still work.
listings.why: Largest plug-in here: 29 electric miles covers most of your daily loop, 5-star NHTSA, midsize cabin. High miles for a PHEV is the main risk.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomiest rear seat of any car on this list and a full-size trunk - the easiest daily child-seat car here.
listings.nextAction: Dealer 4 miles away - it has been listed since May, so there is room to negotiate. Ask for the Carfax and a hybrid battery health check.
listings.why: Toyota hybrid reliability in a midsize body 4 miles from home, 39 mpg, 5-star safety. Priced at the very top of budget, but it has sat a long time.

listings.carSeatNotes: Crossover ride height makes loading a child seat easy; hatch area fits a stroller upright.
listings.nextAction: Dealer - ask for dual-clutch transmission service history and a hybrid battery scan given the 137k miles.
listings.why: Newer Niro than the $7,398 car with only one open recall, but $2,600 more and still 137k miles. Take the 2018 unless this one's history is materially better.

listings.carSeatNotes: Easy hatchback child-seat access, but the small cabin plus limited range makes it a second car rather than the family car.
listings.nextAction: Ask for a LeafSpy battery report before anything else - a 2012 Leaf with a weak pack is worth far less than the asking price.
listings.why: Cheapest EV on the board and mechanically simple, but a 2012 24 kWh pack is likely down to 40-55 real miles, and Colorado winters cut that further. Only viable as a dedicated commuter.

listings.carSeatNotes: Fourth-gen Prius has a genuinely spacious rear seat and a huge hatch - excellent for a child seat plus daycare gear.
listings.nextAction: Two accidents reported - get the full Carfax damage detail and a body-shop inspection before considering it. Also cross-listed on Facebook by the same dealer.
listings.why: Highest mpg on the entire board (56) with Toyota Safety Sense standard and 5-star NHTSA. Held back by 160k miles and two accident records.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - test-fit your rear-facing seat before committing; front-passenger legroom is the constraint.
listings.nextAction: Listed since mid-July with no price movement - message the seller with a below-ask offer and request the VIN and title photo.
listings.why: Zero open recalls, 50 mpg, and it is in Aurora - 5 minutes away. Stale listing means real negotiating room. Size is the only real knock.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize rear seat with plenty of rear-facing clearance and a large trunk.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - the 2011-2014 Sonata Hybrid used a lithium-polymer pack with a mixed reliability record; ask for the VIN and any battery/engine replacement receipts.
listings.why: 83k miles for $7,000 in a 5-star midsize hybrid is good money, but this generation's hybrid system and 2.4L engine are the least proven on this list. Inspect carefully.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan - excellent rear-facing room and a big trunk for the daycare run.
listings.nextAction: 13 recall campaigns exist for the 2016 Fusion - ask the dealer for completion receipts on all of them, especially the steering wheel bolt and door latch campaigns.
listings.why: Newer Fusion Hybrid than the Centennial car at 41 mpg with 5-star safety, but it is $2,600 more and this model year carries an unusually long recall list.

listings.carSeatNotes: Roomy hatchback rear seat with a flat floor and wide doors - the most practical EV shape here for a child seat.
listings.nextAction: Confirm it is the 62 kWh PLUS pack (not the 40 kWh) and get a battery health readout - 111k miles on a passively cooled Leaf pack needs verification.
listings.why: The 62 kWh Plus has real 200+ mile range new, so even a degraded pack easily covers your commute year-round. High miles and a 55-mile drive to Greeley are the catches.

listings.carSeatNotes: Good rear-facing room and a large hatch, though the Prime's rear seat is a 4-seat configuration on this generation.
listings.nextAction: TREAT WITH CAUTION - a 2022 Prius Prime with 62k miles is a $20k+ car; $8,450 is far below any plausible market value. Do not wire money or a deposit. Insist on seeing the car and title in person at a public location.
listings.why: On paper the best car here, which is exactly the problem. It has been listed at this price since 7 August without selling, which is a strong indicator of a bait or fraud listing.
